transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, good to meet you too. Basically, I'm here because I feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next. I just... I can’t really sit idle. And with the new work setup we have right now, it's just made that a lot harder to hide.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?

No, I can't say I've ever had anything like that. I mean, I have trouble sitting still, but I definitely still need my sleep. I haven't noticed any times where I felt super energized or didn't need to sleep.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention on tasks, even when you want to focus?

Yeah, I do. Like... in the longer coaching meetings we have at work, or when I’m reading through a new procedure. I usually start off fine, but after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes kept moving down the page, but I didn’t really take in anything that was said or what I just read. I just lose the thread completely even when I'm trying my best to learn it.
Did you have these same problems with attention or sitting still when you were a child?

Yeah, looking back, this has been around long before my current job setup. When I was in grade school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. They always said I talked out of turn and constantly had to be reminded to stay focused on my work. So, yeah, it's definitely been an issue since I was a kid.
When you lose focus, is it usually because your mind gets pulled into worry?

No, I wouldn't say it's worry. It's not like I'm sitting there stressing about bills or anything like that. My mind just kind of... drifts off. Like I'll start thinking about what I'm going to make for dinner, or a movie I saw last week, or just random things. It's not anxiety, just my brain wandering away from what I'm supposed to be doing.
Do you feel a strong need for things to be done in a very specific, orderly way?

No, not really. I mean... if anything, I'm probably the opposite. I don't really care if things are perfectly organized or done in some strict order. My desk at work is usually a bit of a mess, to be honest. I just kind of take things as they come, so... no, I wouldn't say I need things to be orderly like that.

latest_inference.note: Attention problems and hyperactivity/restlessness began in childhood, persist into adulthood, are not primarily driven by worry, and the patient denies orderliness/perfectionism, ruling against F41.1 and F60.5. Presentation is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive type.
